cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the momentum is being shared as it moves.
cells.act: gather the scattered thoughts into one line
cells.ask: For the next push, write down the one line the whole effort is really for, and keep it where the work can see it.
cells.core:
Your momentum has a center, and it's the kind others can join. When the goal is shared and the meaning is felt, the drive stops being a lone push against resistance and becomes forward motion that carries other people with it. The energy doesn't thin out by being shared. It multiplies, and you can tell on a given day whether the work is heading toward the whole point.

Put the pattern on a page. When you can, set down the one line the effort is really for, so the direction can be seen as well as followed. The pieces of your thinking wander while you push, and the page is where you'll catch them drifting before they cost you a week. Read it to yourself before the next move, then move.
cells.sheetLine: Your momentum carries people, and the point is yours to name.
cells.verb: raise joy together and let a shared meaning carry it outward
cells.place: in the directed momentum toward goals

cells.tense: You will have built something no one asked for, and the building is the point now.
cells.act: keep building the thing with sustained craft
cells.ask: Pick one thing that already has your name on it, and this week give it one honest hour — not a scouting trip, an hour of the actual work.
cells.core:
The celebration has been replaced by the long haul, and the long haul has taken over the room. What was forward motion has become an endless site: the milestone is always next quarter, the push is always on, and the people meant to share the project are now only waiting on it. The momentum is real, and it is running past the point where anyone could stand in it with you.

Some structures fall because they needed to fall, and a real insight is the sledgehammer. Let one piece of the plan run all the way to its end: a small, real completion. Pick the thing that is genuinely yours, and this week give it one honest hour — not a scouting trip, an hour of the actual work. Something meets its edge and holds. The rest of the scaffolding comes down easier after that.

cells.tense: You stood at the door a long time ago, and the door is behind you now.
cells.act: read the hardest page of it twice, slowly, before you stop
cells.ask: For one thing you are pointed at, read or study the hardest page of it twice, slowly, before you stop; let it take as long as it takes.
cells.core:
The drive is still there, but it is not pointed anywhere now. You remember being pulled toward something and being glad to share the pull. That list is not in front of you anymore; the aims that remain are maintenance. Show up, do the day, keep the machine running. Nothing inside the effort is lit, and nothing is rising out of it that wants out.

Depth is the way back, not push. Go all the way into one thing and follow it past where it is comfortable. For a week, take the hard part of what you are already doing and read it twice, slowly, before you stop. No output to show, no one to report to. Follow the thread into the page until your mind finds its own limit in it, and something points again on the far side.

cells.tense: You are already carrying the shared history that holds this group together.
cells.act: bring the two sides of your thinking into one plan
cells.ask: Once this week, write what the group keeps together on one side of a page and what your own direction wants on the other, then draw one line that holds both.
cells.core:
You hold the shared history of a group without calling it holding. You remember the anniversaries and the old arguments, you keep the jokes running, you decide what is worth passing on. The keeping is happening through you. You describe it as just being around, and the people who follow the thread back to its source find your name there and don't say so, because you don't.

Two things are true at once: the belonging wants its rituals, and you have a direction of your own. Rather than let each pull against the other, bring both onto one page — one side what the group keeps, one side what your own motion wants — and draw one line that holds them. A thing held at its real size answers for itself. The plan that can carry both is the next thing you were already going to build.
